title: add VPC control plane provisioning terraform module for AWS (subnets, endpoints, SGs, peering, DNS)
author: Priya Desai
description: This PR introduces a reusable Terraform module and installer integration for provisioning the Redwood Private control plane VPC on AWS. Motivation: customers deploying Private control planes need a secure, well-structured VPC with cross-AZ subnets, private hosted DNS, VPC endpoints for S3/SSM/SecretsManager/ECR, restrictive security groups, and an optional peering/TransitGateway attachment pattern to connect customer workloads. This change encapsulates best-practice networking defaults while exposing configuration knobs for CIDR ranges, AZ placement, endpoint selections, route table overrides, and cross-account peering. The PR touches the terraform module code, environment tfvars for AWS, Helm chart values used by the installer, documentation and end-to-end tests. Backwards compatibility: module defaults are conservative and do not change existing installer behavior unless the new module is referenced in an env. Security considerations: default SGs deny all inbound except control-plane management CIDRs, endpoints are private-by-default, and logs are enabled for route table/flow logs via optional bindings. Upgrade/rollback: module supports create-before-destroy for NAT gateways and route table associations; upgrade notes and rollback plan included. Linear references ENG-7823 and ENG-7890.

release_notes: Added terraform module 'vpc-control-plane' to provision Private control plane VPCs on AWS. Includes subnets across AZs, NAT gateways with create-before-destroy, route tables, VPC endpoints for S3/SSM/SecretsManager/ECR, optional peering/transit-gateway integration, default restrictive security groups, flow logs, and docs. Configurable via env tfvars. Backwards compatible unless opted in.
upgrade_notes: When adopting the new module in an existing installer environment: 1) review and set CIDR and AZ variables to avoid overlap; 2) enable create_before_destroy for NAT gateway replacements to avoid downtime; 3) review 'peering_mode' before enabling peering/transit gateway to avoid unexpected attachments. See redwood-docs/private-deployments/vpc-control-plane.md for full steps.
rollback_plan: If a provisioning apply introduces issues, use terraform state rollback for the module or run 'terraform apply' with the previous tfstate snapshot. For peering/transit-gateway changes, remove the attachment and re-run apply. The module sets default tags and resource names to make state identification deterministic. CI has a smoke-test to validate connectivity; revert the installer's feature flag to disable the module in the worst case.
